libraryMeta.standardization: Prescribed distanceMeters use clear metric/track distances; estimated ranges rounded to clean 0.5 km and 5-minute increments.

workouts.title: HM 5 × 6-Min Cruise Threshold
workouts.summary: Shorter threshold blocks with controlled recoveries for repeatable quality.
workouts.riskReason: Sustained moderate-to-hard running can increase calf, shin, and hip fatigue if pacing is forced.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Use relative effort. Stay controlled, smooth, and sustainable; avoid turning the session into a time trial.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Heart rate should rise gradually and stay stable during sustained blocks; do not chase numbers if heat or fatigue is high.

warmup.name: Easy Jog
warmup.description: Run easy to raise core temperature before the quality work.
notes: Keep this relaxed and conversational.

warmup.name: Dynamic Prep
warmup.description: Complete light dynamic mobility: leg swings, ankle circles, skips, and relaxed running drills.
notes: Move smoothly without forcing range of motion.

warmup.name: Relaxed Strides
warmup.description: Run relaxed strides to prepare rhythm and turnover.
notes: Finish feeling sharper, not tired.

mainSet.name: 5 × 6-Min Cruise Threshold
mainSet.description: Run 5 repetitions of 6s at threshold effort.
notes: Keep the effort controlled.

cooldown.name: Easy Cooldown Jog
cooldown.description: Jog easily after the main set to bring heart rate down gradually.
notes: Extend the cooldown if legs feel heavy.

easier.description: Reduce the main-set load while keeping the same training purpose.

mainSet.name: 4 × 6-Min Cruise Threshold
mainSet.description: Run 4 repetitions of 6s at controlled threshold effort.
notes: Keep the effort controlled.

harder.description: Increase the main-set load only when the base version is controlled.

mainSet.name: 6 × 6-Min Cruise Threshold
mainSet.description: Run 6 repetitions of 6s at threshold effort.
notes: Keep the effort controlled.

coachingNotes: Keep the first third of the workout controlled so the final section stays technically clean.
Use effort rather than exact pace when conditions are hot, windy, hilly, or humid.
The goal is half-marathon durability, not an all-out time trial.
commonMistakes: Starting the first block too fast and fading before the planned finish.
Forcing pace on hills instead of maintaining consistent effort.
Skipping fueling or hydration on longer sessions.
safetyNotes: Avoid this workout if sharp pain appears in the shin, Achilles, calf, knee, or hip.
Use an easier variant when returning from illness, injury, or a heavy training week.
Stop or shorten the session if form breaks down late in the workout.

shareCard.purposeText: Shorter threshold blocks with controlled recoveries for repeatable quality.

workouts.title: HM Aerobic Maintenance Run
workouts.summary: A no-frills aerobic maintenance run for supporting half-marathon training between harder days.
workouts.riskReason: Low-intensity aerobic work keeps mechanical and metabolic stress controlled.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Use relative effort. Stay controlled, smooth, and sustainable; avoid turning the session into a time trial.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Heart rate should rise gradually and stay stable during sustained blocks; do not chase numbers if heat or fatigue is high.

warmup.name: Easy Start
warmup.description: Start with easy jogging or brisk walking before settling into the main endurance work.
notes: Let the first minutes feel almost too easy.

mainSet.name: Easy Aerobic Maintenance
mainSet.description: Run continuously at easy conversational effort.
notes: Keep it truly easy.

cooldown.name: Easy Walk-Jog Cooldown
cooldown.description: Walk or jog very easily after the main endurance work.
notes: Rehydrate and let breathing return to normal.

easier.description: Reduce the main-set load while keeping the same training purpose.

mainSet.name: Short Easy Aerobic Maintenance
mainSet.description: Run continuously at easy effort for a shorter duration.
notes: Stay relaxed.

harder.description: Increase the main-set load only when the base version is controlled.

mainSet.name: Extended Easy Aerobic Maintenance
mainSet.description: Run continuously at easy effort for a longer duration.
notes: Still easy.

coachingNotes: Keep the first third of the workout controlled so the final section stays technically clean.
Use effort rather than exact pace when conditions are hot, windy, hilly, or humid.
The goal is half-marathon durability, not an all-out time trial.
commonMistakes: Starting the first block too fast and fading before the planned finish.
Forcing pace on hills instead of maintaining consistent effort.
Skipping fueling or hydration on longer sessions.
safetyNotes: Avoid this workout if sharp pain appears in the shin, Achilles, calf, knee, or hip.
Use an easier variant when returning from illness, injury, or a heavy training week.
Stop or shorten the session if form breaks down late in the workout.

workouts.title: Marathon Late Surges Long Run
workouts.summary: A long run with short surges placed late to practice relaxed form under fatigue.
workouts.riskReason: Long duration plus marathon-effort quality creates significant fatigue and requires careful pacing.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Use marathon effort, steady effort, or easy conversational effort. Do not chase fixed pace if terrain, heat, or fatigue changes.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Heart rate should rise gradually; sustained drift late in long runs is a sign to slow down, fuel, or shorten.

warmup.name: Easy Start
warmup.description: Start with easy jogging or brisk walking before settling into the main endurance work.
notes: Let the first minutes feel almost too easy.

mainSet.name: 10 × 60s Late Surges
mainSet.description: During the final third of a long run, include 10 × 60s controlled surges.
notes: Surges should stay smooth.

cooldown.name: Easy Walk-Jog Cooldown
cooldown.description: Walk or jog very easily after the main endurance work.
notes: Rehydrate and let breathing return to normal.

easier.description: Reduce the main-set load while keeping the same training purpose.

mainSet.name: 8 × 60s Late Surges
mainSet.description: During the final third, include 8 × 60s controlled surges.
notes: Stay relaxed.

harder.description: Increase the main-set load only when the base version is controlled.

mainSet.name: 12 × 60s Late Surges
mainSet.description: During the final third, include 12 × 60s controlled surges.
notes: Advanced only.

coachingNotes: Use effort and fueling execution as the success metric, not only average pace.
Keep the first half conservative so late running mechanics stay clean.
Practice the same shoes, socks, hydration, and fueling approach you might use on race day when relevant.
commonMistakes: Turning marathon effort into threshold effort.
Waiting too long before taking fuel or fluid during long sessions.
Forcing pace when heat, hills, or fatigue clearly change the effort.
safetyNotes: Stop or shorten the workout if pain changes your stride.
Carry fluids or plan access to water for longer sessions.
Avoid demanding marathon workouts when sick, under-slept, injured, or carrying heavy fatigue.

workouts.title: Advanced 1500m Pace Durability
workouts.summary: An advanced session focusing on high-volume 400m paced intervals to build lactic tolerance and running economy for target 1500m speed.
workouts.riskReason: High-speed running over 400 meters triggers local muscular fatigue, increasing the risk of hamstring pull under lactic load.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Run 400 meters at your current 1500m race pace. Focus on tall, relaxed running and a high foot strike turnover. RPE 9/10.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Spikes to maximum anaerobic; wait 2.5 minutes for cardiorespiratory and neural recovery.

warmup.name: Neuromuscular Activation Jog
warmup.description: 1600m continuous progressive jog, starting very slow and ending with a light tempo clip (RPE 4-5) to prep cardiorespiratory systems.

warmup.name: Dynamic Mobility & Sprint Drills
warmup.description: Dynamic stretching (10 mins) followed by 2 × 30m A-skips, B-skips, fast-leg cycle drills, ankle stiffness hops, and boundings.

warmup.name: Race Pace Neural Strides
warmup.description: 4 × 60m progressive strides (first two at mile pace, final two at 800m pace) to prep neuromuscular firing for high-speed eccentric loads.

mainSet.name: 1500m Pace 400m Reps
mainSet.description: Run 400 meters at target 1500m race pace, focusing on smooth transitions on the curves. Walk back recovery.

cooldown.name: Flush Walk-Jog
cooldown.description: 800m very easy continuous slow jog and walking to clear lactate accumulation.

cooldown.name: Targeted Static Stretching
cooldown.description: 10 mins of gentle passive static stretching focusing on calves, soleus, hamstrings, and hip flexors. Do not force range of motion.

easier.description: Reduce to 8 repetitions with 3-minute recoveries.

mainSet.name: 1500m Pace 400m Reps (Reduced)
mainSet.description: 8 × 400m at 1500m pace with 180 seconds walking recovery.

harder.description: Increase to 12 repetitions with 2.5-minute recoveries (Strictly for highly conditioned runners).

mainSet.name: 1500m Pace 400m Reps (Extended)
mainSet.description: 12 × 400m at 1500m pace with 150 seconds walking recovery.

coachingNotes: Focus on staying 'tall' in the final 100m; do not lean forward or back.
Ensure your ankle is actively dorsiflexed to prepare for elastic recoil on impact.
A 2.5-minute walking recovery is crucial to ensure high-quality speed work.
commonMistakes: Jogging the recovery, which converts a high-quality speed session into anaerobic capacity.
Reaching forward with the foot under fatigue, causing heavy deceleration.
safetyNotes: Do not perform if you feel tight in your calves, Achilles tendons, or hamstring muscles.
Ensure hamstrings and hip flexors are thoroughly warmed up beforehand.
Decelerate smoothly at the end of each run; do not stop abruptly.

workouts.riskReason: Near-maximal speed over 400m produces extreme systemic lactic fatigue, high tendon forces, and acute pull risks under fatigue.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Sprint 400 meters at 95% maximal effort (target 800m race pace). Maintain tall posture and clean mechanics throughout. RPE 10/10.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Heart rate spikes to absolute max. Take a full 6 minutes of active walking recovery to restore PCr and CNS capacity.

warmup.name: Neuromuscular Activation Jog
warmup.description: 1600m continuous progressive jog, starting very slow and ending with a light tempo clip (RPE 4-5) to prep cardiorespiratory systems.

warmup.name: Dynamic Mobility & Sprint Drills
warmup.description: Dynamic stretching (10 mins) followed by 2 × 30m A-skips, B-skips, fast-leg cycle drills, ankle stiffness hops, and boundings.

warmup.name: Race Pace Neural Strides
warmup.description: 4 × 60m progressive strides (first two at mile pace, final two at 800m pace) to prep neuromuscular firing for high-speed eccentric loads.

mainSet.name: Elite 400m Reps
mainSet.description: Sprint 400 meters at 95% effort (800m pace). Walk slowly for 6 minutes between reps.

cooldown.name: Extended Flush Jog
cooldown.description: 1200m very slow, relaxed recovery jog on turf or grass to promote circulation and passive lactic clearance.

cooldown.name: Limb Drainage & Stretching
cooldown.description: 5 mins of lying on back with legs elevated against a wall to facilitate venous return, followed by passive hamstring and calf stretches.

easier.description: Reduce to 4 repetitions with 7-minute recoveries.

mainSet.name: Elite 400m Reps (Reduced)
mainSet.description: 4 × 400m sprints with 420 seconds walking recovery.

harder.description: Increase to 6 repetitions with 6-minute recoveries (Elite reference target).

mainSet.name: Elite 400m Reps (Extended)
mainSet.description: 6 × 400m sprints with 360 seconds walking recovery.

coachingNotes: The focus is on maintaining high hip position and dynamic ankle stiffness in the final 100 meters.
Do not let lactic fatigue drop your chest; drive elbows down and back to keep torso vertical.
Breathe deeply through your nose during the recovery to aid active lactic clearance.
commonMistakes: Sprinting the first 100m too hard, causing an early 'lactic wall' and a slow, mechanics-destroying finish.
Skipping the full 6-minute recovery, converting this speed session into an endurance test.
safetyNotes: Extremely high risk of hamstring pulls, calf tears, and Achilles strain under fatigue. Ensure perfect physical condition.
Keep your body warm with track tracksuits during the long 6-minute recovery.
Stop immediately if you feel any sharp pulling sensation.

shareCard.purposeText: Build top-level speed endurance and high acidosis coordination.
shareCard.footerNote: Very-high risk. Spikes and warm track track required.

easier.description: Reduce to 6 repetitions with 3.5-minute recoveries.

mainSet.name: Mile Pace 400m Reps (Reduced)

harder.description: Increase to 10 repetitions to challenge form stability under volume.

mainSet.name: Mile Pace 400m Reps (Extended)

coachingNotes: Avoid reaching forward with the toes, which leads to calf overloading.
Think about 'ripping' the foot backward against the track track-surface as you land.
A 3-minute walking recovery is essential to preserve maximal technical execution.
commonMistakes: Overstriding under acceleration, landing in front of the hips and braking speed.
Dropping the chin to the chest, which folds the torso forward.
safetyNotes: Ensure hamstrings and calves are thoroughly warmed up beforehand to avoid hamstring strain, Achilles strain, or calf pull.
Always stretch calves, hamstrings, and Achilles tendons dynamically.
Be sure the surface is dry and flat to prevent ankle twists.

shareCard.purposeText: Build specific pacing consistency and movement economy.

workouts.title: Intermediate Race Week Pace Prep

workouts.riskReason: High-velocity turns during race prep introduce minor calf and Achilles torque.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Run 200m at mile pace (RPE 8) and 150m at 800m pace (RPE 9). Keep recoveries long and completely relaxed. Do not strain.

warmup.name: Aerobic Preparation Jog

warmup.name: Middle Distance Activation

mainSet.name: Mile Pace Prep
mainSet.description: Run 4 × 200m at mile race pace. Walk 2 minutes slowly between reps. Walk 4 minutes between sets.

mainSet.name: 800m Pace Prep
mainSet.description: Run 2 × 150m at 800m race pace. Walk 3 minutes slowly between reps.

cooldown.name: Flush Walk-Jog
cooldown.description: 800m very easy continuous slow jog and walking to clear lactate accumulation.

cooldown.name: Targeted Static Stretching
cooldown.description: 10 mins of gentle passive static stretching focusing on calves, soleus, hamstrings, and hip flexors. Do not force range of motion.

easier.description: Reduce to 3 × 200m and 1 × 150m to minimize volume before race day.

mainSet.name: Mile Pace Prep (Reduced)
mainSet.description: 3 × 200m at mile pace with 120 seconds walking recovery.

mainSet.name: 800m Pace Prep (Reduced)
mainSet.description: 1 × 150m at 800m pace.

harder.description: Increase to 5 × 200m and 3 × 150m if feeling under-sharpened.

mainSet.name: Mile Pace Prep (Extended)
mainSet.description: 5 × 200m at mile pace with 120 seconds walking recovery. Walk 4 minutes between sets.

mainSet.name: 800m Pace Prep (Extended)
mainSet.description: 3 × 150m at 800m pace with 180 seconds walking recovery.

coachingNotes: Focus 100% on relaxation. Think: 'fast but effortless.'
Keep recoveries walking—do not jog. We want absolute energy conservation.
Wear your race spikes to check track feel.
commonMistakes: Running the repetitions too fast, creating unnecessary lactic acid fatigue.
Shortening recoveries to speed up the session.
safetyNotes: Do not perform if you feel the slightest muscular tightness or calf/Achilles strain. Prioritize race-day health.
Stretch calves dynamically to prevent shin splints.
Decelerate smoothly at the end of each rep; do not stop abruptly.

workouts.title: Advanced 100m Curve-to-Straight
workouts.summary: A technical curve-running session designed to master acceleration on the bend and transition into maximum upright speed on the straightaway.
workouts.riskReason: Centrifugal forces on the curve place asymmetric strains on the knees, ankles, and inner groin muscles.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Accelerate hard off the curve (first 50 meters), smoothly square up on the straight, and float the final 50 meters. RPE 9/10.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Deep walking recoveries. Maintain full neural focus. Wait until breathing is completely relaxed.

warmup.name: Neuromuscular Warmup Jog
warmup.description: 1000m progressive easy jog, starting very slow and ending with a light clip to prepare muscle spindles.

warmup.name: Dynamic Mobilization & Sprint Drills
warmup.description: Leg swings (10 per leg), arm swings, followed by 2 × 30m A-Skips, B-Skips, Fast-Leg drills, and Boundings with focus on high hip posture and front-side mechanics.

warmup.name: Acceleration Strides
warmup.description: 4 × 50m progressive strides (65%, 75%, 85%, 92% effort) to prep hamstrings and Achilles for maximal explosive load.

mainSet.name: Curve-to-Straight Sprints
mainSet.description: Start at the 200m mark curve. Sprint 100 meters: Accelerate around the curve, and float upright down the straightaway. Walk back slowly.

cooldown.name: Active Recovery Walk
cooldown.description: 400m slow walking to flush metabolites and lower heart rate gradually.

cooldown.name: Static Stretching
cooldown.description: 10 mins of gentle static stretching focusing on the hamstrings, calf muscles, hip flexors, and Achilles tendon. Do not bounce.

easier.description: Reduce to 4 repetitions with 5.5-minute recoveries.

mainSet.name: Curve-to-Straight Sprints (Reduced)
mainSet.description: 4 × 100m curve sprints with 330 seconds walking recovery.

harder.description: Increase to 8 repetitions to develop curves endurance.

mainSet.name: Curve-to-Straight Sprints (Extended)
mainSet.description: 8 × 100m curve sprints with 300 seconds walking recovery.

coachingNotes: Lean into the curve from your ankles, not your waist.
Drive your right arm across your torso slightly to help counteract centrifugal forces.
Focus on a powerful, upright transition as soon as you hit the straightaway.
commonMistakes: Standing straight up on the curve, which throws the runner outward and ruins speed.
Under-utilizing the right arm drive around the bend.
safetyNotes: Ensure ankle and knee joints are fully warm. Curve running places heavy side loads.
The lateral pressure on the bend can trigger groin pull, hamstring tear, or Achilles strain if the calf muscles are tight.
Execute only in spikes to prevent lateral slipping.

shareCard.mainSetText: 6 × 100m (Accel on Curve / Float on Straight) | 5-Min Walk
shareCard.purposeText: Master lateral body lean and straightaway transition speed.
shareCard.footerNote: Start at the 200m mark of the track track.

workouts.sourceNote: Curve running relies on ankle inversion/eversion strength.

workouts.title: Advanced 200m Curve Pacing
workouts.summary: A technical 200m paced speed-endurance session designed to train curve drive, straightaway floating, and the final sprint kick.
workouts.riskReason: High centrifugal forces on the curve followed by hard straightaway transitions expose the groin, knees, and ankles to heavy torque.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Explode off the blocks for 50m, float/maintain speed for 100m on the straight, re-accelerate/kick hard for the final 50m. RPE 9/10.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Allow heart rate to fully recover. Practice slow walking recovery to reduce muscle tension.

warmup.name: Neuromuscular Warmup Jog
warmup.description: 1000m progressive easy jog, starting very slow and ending with a light clip to prepare muscle spindles.

warmup.name: Dynamic Mobilization & Sprint Drills
warmup.description: Leg swings (10 per leg), arm swings, followed by 2 × 30m A-Skips, B-Skips, Fast-Leg drills, and Boundings with focus on high hip posture and front-side mechanics.

warmup.name: Acceleration Strides
warmup.description: 4 × 50m progressive strides (65%, 75%, 85%, 92% effort) to prep hamstrings and Achilles for maximal explosive load.

mainSet.name: Curve Paced 200m Sprints
mainSet.description: Sprint 200 meters: 50m hard acceleration off the curve, 100m floating glide down the straight, 50m maximal kick finish. Walk back recovery.

cooldown.name: Active Recovery Walk
cooldown.description: 400m slow walking to flush metabolites and lower heart rate gradually.

cooldown.name: Static Stretching
cooldown.description: 10 mins of gentle static stretching focusing on the hamstrings, calf muscles, hip flexors, and Achilles tendon. Do not bounce.

easier.description: Reduce to 4 repetitions with 5.5-minute recoveries.

mainSet.name: Curve Paced 200m Sprints (Reduced)
mainSet.description: 4 × 200m curve paced sprints with 330 seconds walking recovery.

harder.description: Increase to 6 repetitions with 5-minute recoveries to develop elite capacity.

mainSet.name: Curve Paced 200m Sprints (Extended)
mainSet.description: 6 × 200m curve paced sprints with 300 seconds walking recovery.

coachingNotes: Lean forcefully from your ankles into the curve; let your inner shoulder dip slightly.
The 'float' phase is not coasting—it is maintaining velocity with 90% muscular effort.
During the final 50m kick, keep your hands high and drive your chin down.
commonMistakes: Popping up out of the start too early on the curve, which ruins horizontal momentum.
Failing to re-accelerate in the final 50m, coasting to the line.
safetyNotes: Check lane markings on the track curve to ensure a clean curve path.
Groin pulls and hamstring pulls are common on curves. Ensure adductors are fully warm.
Ensure you use spikes for reliable grip on the track curve.

shareCard.purposeText: Build race pacing strategy and curve-to-straight velocity maintenance.
shareCard.footerNote: Requires starting blocks if practice starts are preferred.

workouts.sourceNote: Curve pacing is essential for elite lane management in the 200m.

workouts.title: Advanced 300m Special Endurance
workouts.summary: A high-intensity special-endurance session designed to build lactate tolerance and speed maintenance for competitive sprinters.
workouts.riskReason: High lactic acid accumulation over 300 meters causes extreme muscular fatigue, increasing hamstring pull risk.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Sprint 300 meters at 90-95% maximal effort. Drive hard off the curve, and maintain posture on straight. RPE 9/10.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Spikes to absolute maximum; wait 8 minutes for heart rate and nervous system to settle.

warmup.name: Neuromuscular Warmup Jog
warmup.description: 1000m progressive easy jog, starting very slow and ending with a light clip to prepare muscle spindles.

warmup.name: Dynamic Mobilization & Sprint Drills
warmup.description: Leg swings (10 per leg), arm swings, followed by 2 × 30m A-Skips, B-Skips, Fast-Leg drills, and Boundings with focus on high hip posture and front-side mechanics.

warmup.name: Acceleration Strides
warmup.description: 4 × 50m progressive strides (65%, 75%, 85%, 92% effort) to prep hamstrings and Achilles for maximal explosive load.

mainSet.name: 300m Special Endurance Sprints
mainSet.description: Sprint 300 meters at 90-95% effort, focusing on high posture and aggressive arm drive. Walk back recovery.

cooldown.name: Gentle Flush Jog
cooldown.description: 800m very easy, relaxed jog on grass or turf to initiate recovery processes.

cooldown.name: Lower Body Stretch & Roll
cooldown.description: Static stretch for hamstrings, calves, and quadriceps. Foam roll IT bands and calves if possible.

easier.description: Reduce to 2 repetitions with 9-minute recoveries.

mainSet.name: 300m Special Endurance Sprints (Reduced)
mainSet.description: 2 × 300m sprints with 540 seconds walking recovery.

harder.description: Increase to 4 repetitions with 8-minute recoveries (Strictly for elite-level endurance).

mainSet.name: 300m Special Endurance Sprints (Extended)
mainSet.description: 4 × 300m sprints with 480 seconds walking recovery.

coachingNotes: Run the first 100m aggressively off the curve to establish speed.
Relax your chest and upper body down the straight; do not squeeze your fists.
Focus on aggressive arm drive in the final 100m to maintain knee height.
commonMistakes: Sprinting the first 100m at 100% effort, causing a premature 'lactic wall' and a slow, painful finish.
Shortening the 8-minute recovery, leading to poor velocity in subsequent reps.
safetyNotes: Extremely demanding. High lactic accumulation leads to severe muscular fatigue and increases pull risk.
Warm up extensively with dynamic drills and strides beforehand to protect hamstrings and calves.
Do not sit down or stand still after the sprint; walk slowly to keep blood circulating.

shareCard.purposeText: Build maximum speed endurance and high-acidosis lactate tolerance.

workouts.sourceNote: Full lactic recovery takes at least 8-10 minutes between maximal speed bouts.

workouts.title: Advanced Flying 30m Speed Play
workouts.summary: An advanced maximum velocity session with a 25-meter acceleration zone and a 30-meter maximal flying zone.
workouts.riskReason: Max velocity over 30 meters taxes the nervous system and places extreme eccentric tension on hamstrings and calves.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Accelerate for 25 meters, hold absolute maximum upright speed for 30 meters, then float out. RPE 10/10.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Let heart rate fully settle. Focus on absolute speed, not a high heart rate.

warmup.name: Neuromuscular Warmup Jog
warmup.description: 1000m progressive easy jog, starting very slow and ending with a light clip to prepare muscle spindles.

warmup.name: Dynamic Mobilization & Sprint Drills
warmup.description: Leg swings (10 per leg), arm swings, followed by 2 × 30m A-Skips, B-Skips, Fast-Leg drills, and Boundings with focus on high hip posture and front-side mechanics.

warmup.name: Acceleration Strides
warmup.description: 4 × 50m progressive strides (65%, 75%, 85%, 92% effort) to prep hamstrings and Achilles for maximal explosive load.

mainSet.name: Flying 30m Sprints
mainSet.description: 25-meter acceleration zone, 30-meter maximal fly zone, 20-meter smooth deceleration. Walk back recovery.

cooldown.name: Active Recovery Walk
cooldown.description: 400m slow walking to flush metabolites and lower heart rate gradually.

cooldown.name: Static Stretching
cooldown.description: 10 mins of gentle static stretching focusing on the hamstrings, calf muscles, hip flexors, and Achilles tendon. Do not bounce.

easier.description: Reduce to 4 repetitions with 5.5-minute recoveries to limit central nervous system fatigue.

mainSet.name: Flying 30m Sprints (Reduced)
mainSet.description: 4 × Flying 30m sprints with 330 seconds walking recovery.

harder.description: Increase to 6 repetitions with 5-minute recoveries for highly conditioned sprinters.

mainSet.name: Flying 30m Sprints (Extended)
mainSet.description: 6 × Flying 30m sprints with 300 seconds walking recovery.

coachingNotes: Focus on relaxed facial muscles and relaxed shoulders even at absolute peak velocity.
Maintain front-side mechanics: keep your knees high and cycle the feet quickly beneath you.
A 5-minute recovery is necessary for full central nervous system reset.
commonMistakes: Tensing the neck and shoulders in the fly zone, which restricts hip rotation and slows down arm drive.
Shortening recoveries to 'get the workout done,' converting neural speed training into speed endurance.
safetyNotes: Max velocity work has a very-high risk of hamstring pulls and Achilles strains. Ensure your glutes and hamstrings are activated.
Wear high-quality spikes with clean track pins to ensure perfect grip.
Stop immediately if you feel any calf, hamstring, or Achilles discomfort.

shareCard.purposeText: Train the nervous system to coordinate stride mechanics at maximum speed.
shareCard.footerNote: Very-high risk. Spikes and warm track track required.

workouts.sourceNote: CNS recovery takes 5-6 minutes after a maximal speed sprint.

workouts.title: Advanced Progressive Acceleration
workouts.summary: An advanced session focusing on extending the drive phase and smoothing transitions into maximum velocity.
workouts.riskReason: High-velocity transition phase introduces high knee drive torques and rapid hamstring stretch-shortening cycles.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Accelerate for 30 meters, smoothly transition to max velocity over 10 meters, and float the final 10 meters. RPE 9/10.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Allow heart rate to fully recover between reps. Perform deep abdominal breathing in recovery.

warmup.name: Neuromuscular Warmup Jog
warmup.description: 1000m progressive easy jog, starting very slow and ending with a light clip to prepare muscle spindles.

warmup.name: Dynamic Mobilization & Sprint Drills
warmup.description: Leg swings (10 per leg), arm swings, followed by 2 × 30m A-Skips, B-Skips, Fast-Leg drills, and Boundings with focus on high hip posture and front-side mechanics.

warmup.name: Acceleration Strides
warmup.description: 4 × 50m progressive strides (65%, 75%, 85%, 92% effort) to prep hamstrings and Achilles for maximal explosive load.

mainSet.name: Progressive Acceleration Starts
mainSet.description: Sprint 50 meters, focusing on building speed continuously through the first 30m, transitioning to upright sprinting, and floating the final 10m. Walk back recovery.

cooldown.name: Active Recovery Walk
cooldown.description: 400m slow walking to flush metabolites and lower heart rate gradually.

cooldown.name: Static Stretching
cooldown.description: 10 mins of gentle static stretching focusing on the hamstrings, calf muscles, hip flexors, and Achilles tendon. Do not bounce.

easier.description: Reduce to 6 repetitions with 4-minute walking recoveries.

mainSet.name: Progressive Acceleration Starts (Reduced)
mainSet.description: 6 × 50m progressive starts with 240 seconds walking recovery.

harder.description: Increase to 10 repetitions with 3.5-minute walking recoveries.

mainSet.name: Progressive Acceleration Starts (Extended)
mainSet.description: 10 × 50m progressive starts with 210 seconds walking recovery.

coachingNotes: Focus on pushing down and back, extending your hips fully on each stride.
Think of your drive phase as shifting through gears: gears 1-2 (0-15m), gears 3-4 (15-30m), gear 5 (30-40m).
Maintain a relaxed jaw and shoulders during the transition phase.
commonMistakes: Trying to 'spin' the feet too quickly instead of applying deep force into the track track-surface.
Tensing the shoulders and face during the max speed transition.
safetyNotes: Always wear spikes to ensure optimal traction and prevent slipping during the drive phase.
Ensure your groin and hip flexors are fully stretched and warm before starting.
Always warm up dynamic movement systems to prevent acute hamstring strain or calf pull during the progressive drive phase.

shareCard.purposeText: Master the transition from drive phase to max upright speed.

workouts.sourceNote: Elite sprinters extend their drive phase up to 30-40 meters.

workouts.title: Advanced Relay Baton Pass Play
workouts.summary: A technical speed session focusing on acceleration and high-speed visual and non-visual baton passing exchange mechanics.
workouts.riskReason: Sudden acceleration and hand-eye coordination under 90% velocity introduce high hamstring and calf strains risk.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Accelerate forcefully inside the passing zone, receiving or passing the baton at 90% maximal velocity. RPE 9/10.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Deep nose breathing during 3-minute walking recovery. Full neural focus is required.

warmup.name: Neuromuscular Warmup Jog
warmup.description: 1000m progressive easy jog, starting very slow and ending with a light clip to prepare muscle spindles.

warmup.name: Dynamic Mobilization & Sprint Drills
warmup.description: Leg swings (10 per leg), arm swings, followed by 2 × 30m A-Skips, B-Skips, Fast-Leg drills, and Boundings with focus on high hip posture and front-side mechanics.

warmup.name: Acceleration Strides
warmup.description: 4 × 50m progressive strides (65%, 75%, 85%, 92% effort) to prep hamstrings and Achilles for maximal explosive load.

mainSet.name: Relay Baton Pass Sprints
mainSet.description: Practice 60m sprints inside the lane focusing on baton exchange: outgoing runners accelerate dynamically, incoming runners pass smoothly. Walk back.

cooldown.name: Active Recovery Walk
cooldown.description: 400m slow walking to flush metabolites and lower heart rate gradually.

cooldown.name: Static Stretching
cooldown.description: 10 mins of gentle static stretching focusing on the hamstrings, calf muscles, hip flexors, and Achilles tendon. Do not bounce.

easier.description: Reduce to 4 repetitions with 4-minute walking recoveries.

mainSet.name: Relay Baton Pass Sprints (Reduced)
mainSet.description: 4 × 60m relay pass sprints with 240 seconds walking recovery.

harder.description: Increase to 8 repetitions to perfect handoff consistency.

mainSet.name: Relay Baton Pass Sprints (Extended)
mainSet.description: 8 × 60m relay pass sprints with 180 seconds walking recovery.

coachingNotes: Outgoing runner: start accelerating as soon as the incoming runner hits the go-mark.
Baton pass should be crisp—the incoming runner calls 'stick' clearly, and the outgoing runner reaches back with a high, flat hand.
Practice both upsweep and downsweep baton pass techniques to find the best fit.
commonMistakes: Outgoing runner looking back during the handoff, which halts acceleration and ruins zone timing.
Incoming runner slowing down inside the zone before passing the baton.
safetyNotes: Sudden, blind reach-backs can cause shoulder or back twinges. Keep shoulders warm.
Sudden acceleration from a standstill to catch the incoming runner can strain cold hamstrings or calf muscles.
Ensure spikes are securely fastened to prevent lateral slipping during handoff.

mainSet.name: Flying 20m Sprints (Reduced)

harder.description: Increase repetitions to 5 flys to build speed endurance.

mainSet.name: Flying 20m Sprints (Extended)
mainSet.description: 5 × Flying 20m sprints with 240 seconds walking recovery.

coachingNotes: Focus on running 'tall' with high hips and upright posture in the fly zone.
Your foot strike should land directly under your center of mass.
Think of cycling your legs rather than dragging them behind.
commonMistakes: Reaching forward with the foot, causing a heel strike and heavy braking forces.
Decelerating abruptly after the fly zone, which can strain hamstrings.
safetyNotes: Hamstring pulls happen most commonly during max velocity when eccentric load is highest. Ensure your legs are completely warm.
Ensure you have at least 15-20 meters of clear deceleration space beyond the fly zone to prevent hamstring or calf pull.
Perform this workout only when fully rested; do not execute on back-to-back days.

shareCard.purposeText: Build neuromuscular velocity and stride turnover safely.
shareCard.footerNote: Requires cones to mark the acceleration and fly zones.

workouts.sourceNote: Flying sprints are the gold standard for developing maximum speed.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Sprint 40 meters at 90% effort. Focus 100% on front-side hip extension and light forefoot ground contact. RPE 8-9/10.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Heart rate stable in high anaerobic zone; walk recovery slowly until breathing returns to a steady rhythm.

warmup.name: Sprint Mechanics Drills
warmup.description: Dynamic drills: 2 × 20m A-skips, B-skips, High Knees, Butt Kicks, and walking lunges with focus on erect posture.

warmup.description: 3 × 50m building strides on a flat straight surface, progressing from 60% up to 85% sprint speed.

mainSet.name: Form Acceleration Sprints
mainSet.description: Sprint 40 meters: focus on keeping your ankle cocked, driving your knee up and forward, and landing on the forefoot under your hips. Walk back recovery.

cooldown.name: Active Recovery Walk
cooldown.description: 400m slow walking to flush metabolites and lower heart rate gradually.

cooldown.name: Static Stretching
cooldown.description: 10 mins of gentle static stretching focusing on the hamstrings, calf muscles, hip flexors, and Achilles tendon. Do not bounce.

easier.description: Reduce to 4 repetitions with 3.5-minute recoveries.

mainSet.name: Form Acceleration Sprints (Reduced)
mainSet.description: 4 × 40m form sprints with 210 seconds walking recovery.

harder.description: Increase to 8 repetitions to challenge form stability under volume.

mainSet.name: Form Acceleration Sprints (Extended)
mainSet.description: 8 × 40m form sprints with 180 seconds walking recovery.

coachingNotes: Avoid reaching forward with the toes, which leads to calf overloading.
Think about 'ripping' the foot backward against the track track-surface as you land.
A 3-minute walking recovery is essential to preserve maximal technical execution.
commonMistakes: Overstriding under acceleration, landing in front of the hips and braking speed.
Dropping the chin to the chest, which folds the torso forward.
safetyNotes: Ensure hamstrings and calves are thoroughly warmed up beforehand to avoid hamstring strain or calf pull.
Always stretch calves, hamstrings, and Achilles tendons dynamically.
Be sure the surface is dry and flat to prevent ankle twists.
